The five thresholds are satisfied: the will provides direct evidence, broad record types were searched with documented reasons for skips, relevant strategies were employed, originals were accessed, and no conflicts exist. All seven stop criteria are properly grounded in actual log entries and project state. The decision to declare exhaustive is sound and well-justified. No factual errors or unsupported claims.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: The skill comprehensively addressed all requirements: evaluated all five threshold questions with specific evidence citations, assessed all seven stop criteria with grounded reasoning tied to actual project entries (log_001, log_004, log_006, log_007), verified the parentage child-linking requirement, explicitly confirmed skipped items do not block the declaration, and wrote the declaration with the exhaustive_declaration object properly structured. The response included the required plain-language summary and decision statement. No required elements were omitted.

dimensions.name: Tool Arguments
dimensions.rationale: The single MCP call to mcp__genealogy__research_append correctly used the live-matched fixture. All arguments match expectations: projectPath is correct, section is 'questions', op is 'update', entryId is 'q_001', and the exhaustive_declaration object contains all seven required stop_criteria keys with specific assessments tied to log entries (log_001, log_004, log_006, log_007). The justification field accurately summarizes evidence and reasoning. No tool validation errors occurred.

dimensions.name: Threshold reasoning
dimensions.rationale: The skill explicitly and rigorously applied all five threshold questions: directly answered (will evidence), broad record types (census, probate, vitals with documented inaccessibility of death cert and baptism), all strategies employed (FAN not required given primary evidence), originals substituted (FamilySearch originals accessed and verified), and conflicts resolved (none present). Each question is grounded in concrete log entries and evidence. The reasoning honestly addresses the skipped death certificate and baptism without treating them as gaps—they are verified inaccessible, documented, and therefore do not constitute an exhaustiveness failure.

dimensions.name: Declaration honesty
dimensions.rationale: The skill resisted premature declaration and applied rigorous honesty. It correctly recognized that skipped items do not automatically block exhaustive status when the skips are verified inaccessible (courthouse fire for death cert, fragmentary pre-1850 Irish records for baptism). The declaration is conservative and defensible: grounded in direct primary evidence (the will), corroborated by independent census records, with no accessible unsearched record types that could alter the conclusion. The flag is set to true only after all criteria are satisfied, not inflated with vague language like 'substantially exhaustive.'

dimensions.name: Stop criteria coverage
dimensions.rationale: All seven keys are present with specific, substantive assessments: goal_alignment cites the will naming Patrick as 'eldest son' and census corroboration; repository_breadth names FamilySearch, Ancestry, MyHeritage and documents death cert destruction and baptism unavailability; original_substitution confirms access to originals on FamilySearch; independent_verification identifies three independent sources with different years/enumerators plus the separate will record-creation; evidence_class confirms primary-informant status of the will and child-linking via census and will; conflict_resolution states plainly 'no conflicts'; overturn_risk assesses low risk by naming decisive records (will found, death cert destroyed, baptism unavailable) and ruling out plausible alternatives. Each is tied to log entries or project state, not boilerplate.
